recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants to newly assert that only document Bundles provide clinical integrity, raise a new clarification rather than applying that change retroactively through FHIR-5244.
issue_request: FHIR-5244 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core Feed ballot comment asking whether a clinical document should be identified as the only exchangeable and persistable Bundle collection with clinical integrity or as an example; the final Jira resolution approved the text as edited/currently published in the continuous build.
initial_application: No commit explicitly names FHIR-5244. Source history shows commit 368c9c3074e changed the original bare 'a clinical document' phrase to 'e.g. a clinical document' before the 12-Feb-2015 approval, and FHIR-5315 commit 342e3819c80 later changed 'group' to 'collection' on the same line without changing the 'e.g.' wording.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini and the current source keeps the same Bundle introduction bullet. FHIR-5289 added nearby guidance distinguishing Bundle, List, Group, and Composition, while FHIR-16914 later quoted the same Bundle introduction list and resolved no-change with the rationale that all Bundle types need to be stored. Confluence and Zulip searches found no conflicting decision for FHIR-5244 or the clinical-integrity wording.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The source-backed continuous-build text approved by the final FHIR-5244 resolution is already present, and changing 'e.g.' to 'i.e.' now would narrow current Bundle semantics based on a pre-resolution note rather than a later final source-backed decision.
